sec: CTID pathology & etiology (ciliopathies to metabolic) · p793

items.q: The pathology of chronic tubulointerstitial disease is:
opts: Scarring with tubulointerstitial fibrosis and atrophy of more than 5%
Segmental sclerosis of the glomerular tuft only
items.exp: Pathology of CTID: scarring + tubulointerstitial fibrosis & atrophy (>5%), illustrated by the histopathology figure. (Book p793)

items.q: Which of the following is the first listed etiology of chronic tubulointerstitial disease?
items.exp: The etiology list begins with ciliopathies, followed by reflux nephropathy (VUR), obstructive nephropathy, drugs, toxins and metabolic causes. (Book p793)

items.q: Fill up: Reflux nephropathy, listed second among the etiologies, is due to ______.
items.exp: Etiology 2 of CTID: reflux nephropathy (VUR — vesicoureteric reflux). (Book p793)

items.q: Match each drug with its characteristic CTID lesion — 1) Lithium  2) Calcineurin inhibitors  3) Proton pump inhibitors … A) Striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis  B) Microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation  C) Listed as a drug causing CTID
items.exp: Drugs in CTID: lithium — microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation; calcineurin inhibitors — striped pattern, afferent arteriolar hyalinosis; PPIs also listed. (Book p793)

items.q: A patient on long-term lithium develops renal impairment. The biopsy is expected to show:
opts: Microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation
Striped pattern of fibrosis with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis
items.exp: Lithium: microcystic changes in distal tubules without interstitial inflammation. The striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis is a calcineurin-inhibitor effect. (Book p793)

items.q: A renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus has progressive renal dysfunction. The characteristic histological pattern is:
opts: Striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis
Microcystic change in distal tubules without inflammation
items.exp: Calcineurin inhibitors (–) produce a striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis. (Book p793)

items.q: Match each toxin with its CTID syndrome — 1) Lead  2) Cadmium … A) Ouch Ouch nephropathy  B) Saturnine gout with hyperuricemia
items.exp: Toxins: lead — saturnine gout with hyperuricemia; cadmium — ouch ouch nephropathy. (Book p793)

items.q: Fill up: Cadmium toxicity causes the so-called ______ nephropathy.
items.exp: Toxins in CTID: lead — saturnine gout/hyperuricemia; cadmium — 'ouch ouch nephropathy'. (Book p793)

items.q: A battery-recycling worker has gout with hyperuricemia and renal impairment. Which toxin is implicated?
items.exp: Lead causes saturnine gout with hyperuricemia; cadmium causes ouch ouch nephropathy. (Book p793)

items.q: Match the metabolic cause of CTID with its named entity — 1) Hyperuricemia  2) Hypokalemia … A) Vacuolization of PCT > DCT  B) Urate nephropathy
items.exp: Metabolic causes of CTID: hypercalcemia, hyperuricemia (urate nephropathy), hyperoxaluria and hypokalemia (vacuolization of PCT > DCT). (Book p793)

items.q: Hypokalemia in CTID produces vacuolization of the proximal convoluted tubule more than the distal convoluted tubule.
opts: False — vacuolization affects the DCT more than the PCT
False — hypokalemia causes no tubular change
True, but only when hypercalcemia coexists
items.exp: Metabolic etiology list: hypokalemia — vacuolization of PCT > DCT. (Book p793)

items.q: The histology figures for urate nephropathy and for IgG4 disease in this section both carry an arrow pointing to:
opts: Fibrosis, with the disease name printed beneath each figure
Tubular atrophy, with glomerular sparing noted in the label
An interstitial infiltrate, with normal glomeruli in both panels
Basket-weave lamellation of the lamina densa on electron microscopy
items.exp: The histology figures are labelled CTID histopathology (fibrosis, tubular atrophy), urate nephropathy (fibrosis) and IgG4 disease (fibrosis). (Book p793)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed causes of chronic tubulointerstitial disease. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Listed etiologies: ciliopathies, reflux nephropathy (VUR), obstructive nephropathy, drugs, toxins and metabolic causes plus autoimmune diseases. (Book p793)
